conviction_note: The half-year's net sales and adjusted EBIT were pre-released by ad-hoc on 2026-09-07 (the stock rose 6.49% on 09-08 and has since given all of it back), and the FY guide was explicitly maintained in that same ad-hoc three weeks ago, so a guidance change on 09-29 is unlikely. The move sits near the pre-released base of about 3%, and the direction is close to a coin flip. The only unpriced lean is a small negative: 111 insolvent competitor stores are running a clearance sale in Hornbach's home market during its Q3, and the company has not yet said how that affects it.

already_public.what: Q2 and 6M 2026/27 preliminary figures by ad-hoc (MAR Art. 17). Q2 net sales EUR 1,813.7m (+7.3%), Q2 adj. EBIT EUR 124.6m (+12.8%), 6M net sales EUR 3,816.2m (+6.0%), 6M adj. EBIT EUR 285.6m (+4.9%). Includes a +1.3 business-day calendar effect.

FY 2026/27 guide maintained in the same ad-hoc: net sales at or slightly above EUR 6,433.9m, adj. EBIT at the prior-year level of EUR 264.7m (±5%, so EUR 251.5-277.9m). 6M adj. EBIT of 285.6 already exceeds the top of that range, so the guide implies H2 adj. EBIT of at most about -7.7m, against -7.5m in H2 2025/26. The German press already calls the guide 'vorsichtig' (cautious) and says there is 'Spielraum nach oben' (room to the upside).

Six Hellweg stores to be taken over (subject to Bundeskartellamt review and court approval of the insolvency plan), with reopening as Hornbach stores in spring 2027. Quirin reiterated Buy with a EUR 110 target on 09-22, and the stock rose 3.73% that day.
Berenberg Hold, EUR 90 target, after the preliminary figures: the strong quarter underpins the 2026/27 targets.

new_in_release.expect: Most likely reiterated, since it was maintained by ad-hoc on 09-07 citing geopolitical and sourcing/logistics cost risks. There is a small chance (about 15%) of an upgrade to 'slightly above' or a pointer to the upper end, because H1 already exceeds the FY adj. EBIT range. A plain reiteration is what the 09-08 to 09-28 fade already reflects.

unknown, leaning slightly negative. September trading has been against 111 Hellweg/BayWa clearance-sale stores (about 30% off the whole range since early September). Any Q3 commentary may be cautious, although management may frame it as share gains after the stores close at the end of November.
unknown. H1 2025/26 capex more than doubled (EUR 106.7m against 51.2m), and expansion (Serbia, Austria, Hellweg sites) continues. Inventory and working capital are not yet public.

findings.finding: Insolvent competitors Hellweg and BayWa Bau & Garten have been running clearance sales in 111 German DIY stores since early September, at about 30% off the whole range, with stores that find no buyer closing by the end of November 2026. This is a direct price and traffic headwind in Hornbach's home market during Q3 (Sep-Nov). It gives management a concrete reason to keep the outlook cautious rather than lift it on the H1 overshoot.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H2 earnings commentary has been punished here: the Q3 2025/26 ad-hoc of 2025-12-05 ('Reduced earnings in Q3') took the stock down 7.34% on 2025-12-08, and the 2024-12-20 Q3 release fell 11.25% (Yahoo daily bars). Plain guide reiterations on pre-released report days moved 1-2% (2025-12-19 -1.75%, 2026-05-19 +1.79%).
findings.original_quote: Seit Anfang September läuft in weiten Teilen des Filialnetzes der Abverkauf. Aktuelle Angaben nennen 111 Hellweg- und BayWa-Bau-&-Garten-Märkte, in denen Warenbestände verkauft werden. [...] Märkte ohne Käufer sollen nach den bisherigen Planungen spätestens bis Ende November 2026 schließen. (Translation: Since early September the clearance sale has been running across large parts of the store network. Current figures name 111 Hellweg and BayWa Bau & Garten stores in which inventory is being sold. [...] Stores without a buyer are to close by the end of November 2026 at the latest.)
findings.why_not_priced: English coverage of Hornbach since 09-07 is the pre-release and the store-takeover news, which is the positive side of the same insolvency. The clearance sale is reported only in the German consumer and regional press (t-online, ms-aktuell, agrarzeitung). If the market had priced the Q3 headwind, the 09-18 and 09-22 takeover news should not have lifted the stock (+1.84% and +3.73%). But the stock has given back the whole +6.49% pre-release gain since 09-08, which may already contain some of it. The transmission to Hornbach's margin is a hypothesis the company has not confirmed, hence the small size.
findings.independence: t-online (2026-09-17/18) independently reports 68 Hellweg and 43 BayWa stores in clearance with 'teils stark reduziert' (partly sharply reduced) prices: https://www.t-online.de/finanzen/aktuelles/wirtschaft/id_101440578/insolvente-baumarkt-riesen-raeumungsverkauf-laeuft-bundesweit.html. Same underlying event, different outlet; nothing from Hornbach itself.

outside_window.finding: Takeover of six Hellweg stores (Ahrensfelde, Berlin-Köpenick, Dortmund-Kley, Essen-Borbeck, Freiberg, St. Augustin), subject to Bundeskartellamt review and court approval of the insolvency plan, with handover in early December 2026 and reopening in spring 2027. The share gain after Hellweg closes at the end of November is the positive counterpart of the finding above.
Q3 2026/27 (Sep-Nov) figures, which will show how the clearance-sale competition and the post-closure share gain net out. The Q3 ad-hoc last year came on 2025-12-05.

German finance press (finanzen.net, ms-aktuell) spells out that the maintained guide is 'vorsichtig' (cautious) with 'Spielraum nach oben' (room to the upside), which makes explicit that a mere reiteration is the market's base case. English wire copy repeated the ad-hoc without that framing.
The German BHB sector data (H1 2026 -0.4%, June +5.8% on heat) had no English equivalent, but it only corroborates the pre-released Q2 and moved no number.
lessons_applied: 'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company has said it': cut the Hellweg clearance-sale finding from -0.15 to -0.1 and widened its range upward to +1.0, because Hornbach has not said the clearance sale touches its Q3 and may frame the insolvency as share gains.

'A finding about a number already told is worth 0' and 'the move is in the guide': confirmed the draft's choice to carry no reported_quarter finding and to keep abs_move at the pre-released base of 3.0 rather than the 7-9% new-numbers or guidance-change bases. The guide was maintained by ad-hoc three weeks before.
'A truncated zero is not evidence nobody is short' and 'anchor_covered false means no positioning anchor': rewrote positioning_check to say this explicitly rather than 'no short interest'.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': added cash_flow/working capital to new_in_release as an unknown line (last year's H1 capex doubled). No size, because nothing about it is sourced.
